name: LLM RAG service patterns no notebook sprawl
short_definition: Production AI lives in FastAPI (or worker) services with versioned HTTP contracts, not Jupyter notebooks or ad-hoc scripts. Python owns LLM/RAG orchestration: retrieve → filter → rerank → generate, with SSE streams, cost/auth gates, and typed Pydantic I/O. Next/TS is the product shell/BFF; Python is the AI peer service. As of 2026-07-13: FastAPI 0.139.x + httpx + optional LiteLLM gateway + Temporal for multi-step agents.
scope_in: FastAPI AI service layout (chat, RAG search/ingest, embeddings, tools)
Production RAG pipeline layers (chunk, embed, store, retrieve, filter, rerank, generate)
Request/response contracts, streaming (SSE), auth, rate limits, cost metering
Service boundary vs Next BFF vs workers vs durable workflows
Observability for LLM calls (trace ids, token usage, latency)
Anti-notebook / no-colab-as-product rule for shippable systems
scope_out: Jupyter research notebooks for offline eval only (not deploy path)

defaults.surface: Dedicated FastAPI AI service (or clearly named package under monorepo services/ai)
defaults.api: Versioned routes: POST /v1/chat, /v1/chat/stream, /v1/rag/query, /v1/ingest; OpenAPI is contract
defaults.schemas: Pydantic v2 request/response; never raw dict bodies for public AI routes
defaults.stream: SSE via fastapi.sse EventSourceResponse for tokens (py-streaming-sse)
defaults.llm_access: Call via internal LiteLLM proxy or thin provider client with timeouts; no keys in frontend
defaults.rag: Process→chunk→embed→store; query→filter→(rerank)→generate; cite sources in response schema
defaults.workers: Heavy ingest/embed on queue workers; API stays thin and cancelable
defaults.state: Conversation/message rows in Postgres/Supabase; vectors in pgvector or managed vector store
defaults.deploy: Container + ASGI (uvicorn/granian); health /readyz; never notebook server

use_python_ai_service_when: Product needs RAG, multi-step tool use, or provider-agnostic LLM orchestration
Secrets and spend must stay server-side
Same team already owns Python workers/data stack
keep_in_next_only_when: Trivial one-shot completion with Vercel AI SDK and no private corpus
No server-side retrieval or tool sandbox required
split_service_when: AI latency/cost isolation from main API
Different scale profile (GPU/embed workers vs CRUD API)
do_not: Ship notebooks, Gradio demos, or Streamlit as the production AI surface
Put provider API keys in browser or Next public env
Block API event loop with sync embedding of large corpora

do: Auth + rate limit + max_tokens/max_duration on every AI route
Propagate request_id/traceparent into LLM and vector calls
Return structured citations (doc_id, chunk_id, score) for RAG answers
Cancel upstream generation on client disconnect
Version prompts and model names in config (settings), not hardcode in handlers
Separate ingest pipeline from online query path
dont: Don't use notebooks as long-running product servers
Don't dump entire vector DB into the prompt
Don't share one global AsyncClient without timeouts
Don't log full prompts/completions with PII at info level
Don't treat LangChain graphs as a substitute for HTTP auth/quotas
Don't run unbounded agent loops on the request thread without timeouts

code_skeleton:
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException
from fastapi.sse import EventSourceResponse, ServerSentEvent
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings

class Settings(BaseSettings):
    llm_base_url: str = "http://litellm:4000"
    llm_api_key: str
    max_prompt_chars: int = 8000
    model: str = "gpt-4o-mini"

settings = Settings()  # type: ignore[call-arg]
app = FastAPI(title="ai-service")

class ChatIn(BaseModel):
    conversation_id: str | None = None
    message: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=8000)

class RagHit(BaseModel):
    doc_id: str
    chunk_id: str
    score: float
    text: str

class RagAnswer(BaseModel):
    answer: str
    citations: list[RagHit]

async def current_user() -> str:
    return "user_123"  # real JWT dep

User = Annotated[str, Depends(current_user)]

async def retrieve(q: str, user: str) -> list[RagHit]:
    # vector search + tenant filter; mock
    return [RagHit(doc_id="d1", chunk_id="c1", score=0.9, text="...")]

@app.post("/v1/rag/query", response_model=RagAnswer)
async def rag_query(body: ChatIn, user: User) -> RagAnswer:
    if len(body.message) > settings.max_prompt_chars:
        raise HTTPException(400, "prompt too large")
    hits = await retrieve(body.message, user)
    # call LLM with context + hits; return answer + citations
    return RagAnswer(answer="...", citations=hits)

@app.post("/v1/chat/stream", response_class=EventSourceResponse)
async def chat_stream(body: ChatIn, user: User) -> AsyncIterator[ServerSentEvent]:
    # stream tokens from gateway; yield token/error/done events
    yield ServerSentEvent(data={"token": "hi"}, event="token")
    yield ServerSentEvent(raw_data="[DONE]", event="done")
failure_modes: Notebook or Streamlit demo promoted to prod without auth/quotas
Prompt injection exfiltrating tools or other tenants' chunks
Unscoped vector search leaking cross-tenant documents
Cost runaway: no max tokens, no concurrency cap, no disconnect cancel
Stale embeddings after content updates without reindex job
Blocking sync SDK on event loop → API latency collapse
Oversized context window stuffing → OOM or provider 413
Missing citations → untrustworthy answers in product UX
anti_patterns: Architecture centered on .ipynb files as the service
Monolithic 'god agent' route with unbounded tool recursion
RAG = embed query + top-k only, no ACL filter on chunks
Ingest on the request path for multi-MB docs without a job
Copy-paste Colab secrets into committed configs
Using BackgroundTasks alone for critical multi-step agents

optional_orch: LangGraph only when graph state is justified

deprecation_watch: Notebooks / Streamlit / Gradio as production AI architecture
LangChain as mandatory framework for every chat endpoint
Sync OpenAI SDK without to_thread in async FastAPI handlers
Unbounded agent while True loops on request workers
ts_boundary: Next.js owns UI, session cookies, and product BFF. Call Python AI over internal network with user JWT or service token; stream via fetch ReadableStream → browser. Do not reimplement RAG in Route Handlers when corpus/ACL lives in Python. Share OpenAPI types (orogen/openapi-ts). Vercel AI SDK ok for thin public demos; production private data stays on Python.
rust_boundary: Stay in Python for orchestration, RAG, and provider SDKs. Hand off to Rust only for ultra-hot non-LLM gateways, binary protocol edges, or measured CPU bottlenecks — not default for AI product logic.
supabase_boundary: Store conversations, message audit, doc metadata, and pgvector chunks with tenant_id. Online path uses service_role in Python with explicit tenant filters — never trust client-supplied tenant alone. RLS for user-facing reads of chat history; workers use service role. Prefer DB-backed citations over ephemeral notebook state.
boundary_contracts: OpenAPI for all AI HTTP routes (chat, stream events, RAG)
SSE event schema: token|error|done (+ citation events optional)
Env: LLM_BASE_URL, LLM_API_KEY, MODEL, DATABASE_URL, VECTOR_*
Ingest job payload schema versioned when async
Auth: Bearer JWT; document scopes for ai:chat vs ai:ingest

decision_matrix_row.python: FastAPI AI service + workers; gateway for providers
decision_matrix_row.ts: Next UI/BFF, stream consumer, session — not private RAG core
decision_matrix_row.rust: Optional edge proxy only when measured

threats: Prompt injection → tool abuse or data exfiltration
Cost DoS via unauthenticated or unlimited generation
Secret leakage in logs, traces, or error messages
Supply-chain risk from heavy AI dependency trees
Indirect prompt injection via retrieved documents
mitigations: AuthN/Z + per-user rate limits and concurrency caps
Tenant-scoped retrieval filters mandatory before prompt assembly
Output/tool allowlists; human confirm for destructive tools
Redact PII in LLM observability backends
Pin deps with uv.lock; audit new AI packages
Treat retrieved text as untrusted input to the model

must_generate: FastAPI service with Pydantic I/O and auth deps
SSE stream pattern for chat tokens when streaming UX required
Tenant filter on any vector/SQL retrieval
OpenAPI-documented routes — no notebook deploy path
must_not_generate: Unscoped similarity search across all tenants
Agent loops without max steps/time budget
Ingest of large files entirely inside request handler without queue

tests_required: Contract tests for chat/RAG request schemas
Mocked LLM failure → error event or 502 mapping
ci_gates: Grep ban for notebook deploy / hardcoded sk- keys in src

positive: FastAPI app under services/ai or similar
negative: streamlit run / gradio launch as prod entry

skill_module_bullets: AI = FastAPI peer service, not notebooks or Streamlit product surface
Python owns RAG + LLM orchestration; Next owns UI/BFF/session
RAG prod path: chunk→embed→store; query→filter→rerank→generate + citations
Auth, rate limits, max tokens, disconnect cancel on every AI route
Stream tokens with fastapi.sse; persist final messages to Postgres
Heavy ingest/embed on workers; thin cancelable API
